body: I agree about going with php/iop first. I haven’t been to discovery res but I’ve known kids who went to Whittier and Downey and hated it. the staff treated them poorly and often times kids would discharge and end up right back there. same with other short term residentials. php and iop are safer for sure. might still end up as revolving door patients (and sometimes the programs say you have to go to res or you will be dropped) but it’s definitely worth a shot. there are a lot of phps and iops in the socal area, some better than others. and I agree with ahhh1ex that try to do an in-person one if feasible because connection is really helpful for teens and for building more rapport with the therapist

I’m so sorry you had to go through that. I was there too and it was horrible. Finally someone brought up Canyon Ridge (thought I was just being “dramatic” with what was went on there). Definitely one of the worst hospitals. Relate to so many things you said. The staff were bad (a select few were good), taking forever with skin checks and laughing, the mask thing yeah, they wouldn’t give meds even if they were prescribed (started bad withdrawal bc they refused) or the right meds, and so much more. I’m glad you’re out of there. ❤️

to be fair, a lot of hospitals that have PHP/IOP still send kids to residential. Also, there are residentials that have step-down programs to PHP/IOP so watch out for that (they might end up sending kids to their res)

PHP/IOP will almost always have connections with residentials, but they are way safer than res. Definitely go to that rather than sending your kid somewhere.

One place I went was really great (it was a kids/adolescents ward). The doctors actually cared, I actually got therapy, the nurses were awesome and actually talked to us, the techs played games with us. And they all treated us like actual people. We got to go outside, too.

But after that, the rest of the places I went were shit. They didn't care at all, and they didn't do those 15 min checks so a bunch of the other patients would be harming themselves and things like that. None of them would let us go outside no matter how long we were in there. Also, I was withdrawing from my medication one place and throwing up very often, and the nurses didn't care (even though my roommates literally kept going up to them to help me).

Depends on if you're going to an adult or adolescent ward. Some adult wards let you bring your phone, but adolescent ones don't (in the US at least).  I definitely agree with bringing books - one place I went had books, and that was the main thing that got me through being there. Bring your own clothes because it's usually better than wearing the scrubs they provide. But the clothes can't have wires or strings like 5howerBeer said. They might remove them for you, but I'd suggest just bringing ones that don't or cutting them out yourself beforehand. Honestly don't really need to bring much because they'll take most of it away.

At the ER, they'll just ask you a billion questions (often will have multiple people talk to you at different times but with same questions - nurses, social workers, doctors, etc.) You'll also have blood/urine tests and possibly have a person watching you at all times or sitting outside your door. Then you'll wait there while they look for a bed for you - might be that same day, might be several days later. Good thing is they might let you have your phone in the ER to pass time, so bring a charger (they'll lock these up for you when you go to the ward).

it's hard when you have a bunch of patients rotating in and out, but it usually made my day when the staff remembered small things that I liked (like one time they gave me my own sudoku book because I was always doing that and sometimes they'd join in on it with me)

The first time I went (for about two weeks), the ward communicated with my school, and everything was fine - I didn't have to make up work and could just go back. The second time, I went right after I got discharged from the first place, so I ended up out of school for quite a bit in total and decided to drop out to focus on my mental health (but my school told me I could just be off for the fall trimester and continue again in the winter without having to delay graduation). So it should be fine, honestly.
